prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: CNC(=O)c1cc(Oc2ccc(NC(=O)Nc3ccc(Cl)c(C(F)(F)F)c3)cc2)ccn1
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL279

Assay A:
  Description: Inhibition of VEGFR2 (unknown origin) after 30 mins by HTRF assay
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibition of VEGFR-2 (unknown origin) using biotinylated poly-GluTyr (4:1) as substrate after 5 mins by ELISA
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE" | "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
raw: {"call": "INSUFFICIENT_INFO", "confidence": 0.45, "error_class": "assay_method", "reason": "The two assays use different detection technologies (HTRF vs ELISA), different substrates, and different incubation times (30 min vs 5 min), which can shift IC50 values in either direction; for a potent reference compound like sorafenib these differences may or may not exceed 0.3 log units, making a definitive call uncertain."}

parsed.reason: The two assays use different detection technologies (HTRF vs ELISA), different substrates, and different incubation times (30 min vs 5 min), which can shift IC50 values in either direction; for a potent reference compound like sorafenib these differences may or may not exceed 0.3 log units, making a definitive call uncertain.
